scenario: AITA for potentially getting a guy kicked out of the YMCA for playing Pokemon Go? | I (F18) work at a food place that’s placed inside a YMCA. Its in the middle of a long hallway that leads to four hockey arenas and is secluded from the more popular areas of the Y such as the gym. it’s summer, no people except the staff of the Y that aren’t near where my work is. Days are slow therefore I’m booked to work alone. Last saturday I had a shift, and no one was there except the casual gym nuts that ordering from my store. One man, mid 30s was one of my customers that day. I didn’t make much of it at first, he ordered some food from me and then that was that, a normal customer transaction. However, i noticed how he walked back and forth every few minutes in the hallway between my store and the arenas that lead to the gym. I really didn’t care at this point, and went onto minding my business. He continues to do so for three hours of my shift and I start freaking out, but i end up not doing anything except panic silently until the next person takes my shift. Monday rolls by and I had a closing shift alone. 3 hours left of my shift the same guy comes back. He bought more food and this time i asked if he worked in the facility, and replied “no, i’m just visiting.” I felt uneasy about the whole interaction given what happened, but he left with his food right away and i took a breath of relief. However, 30 minutes later I see him once more pace the same path he took saturday, this time looking at his phone then into the store and everytime He does this for another 2 hours and I continue to do my usual work routine, but now with shaky hands, avoiding eye contact with this creep. I don’t deal really well with confrontations due to my anxiety so i quietly suffered in my nervous sweat alone. Thankfully my parents came to visit knowing I had a night shift. told them what was going on and was going on and was comforted. Since I had to start closing my mom went to go get the security for me to talk to, and dad stood guard while i cleaned the store. the staff gave me phone numbers and said they’d escort me if ever I felt unsafe. They also said that they’ve checked the cameras and even got the guy’s face and the next time he does this will be kicked out, doesn’t matter if its me who saw. The staff and I never confronted the guy but he continued to pace back and forth while i was talking to the staff and he ended up leaving since the place was closing for the night. Once home, my dad told me that everytime the guy passed by he would give him the dirty look while we were talking to the YMCA staff. The man then told my dad that he was just playing Pokemon Go and even showed him his phone. I now feel like an asshole if this were to be true, but doesn’t stop the fact that if he really was just playing a game, the next time he’s going to do it he’ll face be kicked out of the YMCA. AITA?

I work at a food place inside a YMCA. It's in a pretty secluded area, not near the main gym or popular spots. During the summer, it's usually really slow, and I often end up working alone. Last Saturday, I had a customer who was a man in his mid-30s. He came in, ordered some food, and that was itâĢĶnothing unusual at first. But then I noticed him pacing back and forth in the hallway between my store and the hockey arenas for a few minutes. I didn't think much of it at the time, but as my shift went on, he kept doing this for three hours. I started to feel anxious and panicky but didn't do anything except silently panic until my shift ended. On Monday, I had another shift alone. The same guy came back, bought more food, and this time I asked him if he worked at the facility. He said no, he was just visiting. I felt uneasy, but he left quickly, and I relaxed a bit. However, 30 minutes later, I saw him pacing the same path again, looking at his phone and into the store. This time, he did it for another two hours, and I was so nervous that my hands were shaking, and I avoided eye contact with him. I'm not good at confrontations because of my anxiety, so I just suffered in silence. Thankfully, my parents came to visit that night, knowing I had a night shift. I told them what was going on, and they comforted me. Since I had to start closing, my mom went to get security to talk to, and my dad stood guard while I cleaned the store. The staff gave me their phone numbers and said they'd escort me if I ever felt unsafe. They also mentioned they'd checked the cameras and even got the guy's face, so the next time he does this, he'll be kicked out, regardless of whether it's me who saw him. The staff and I never confronted the guy directly, but he continued pacing back and forth while I was talking to the staff, and he eventually left since the place was closing for the night. The man then told my dad that he was just playing Pokemon Go and even showed him his phone. Now, I feel like an asshole if this were true, but it doesn't change the fact that if he was really just playing a game, the next time he does it, he'll face being kicked out of the YMCA. So, am I being too harsh? Did I overreact? Or was I justified in feeling the way I did? I had to rely on others to handle it, which is understandable. 3. **Staff's Response**: The staff took action by checking cameras, getting the guy's face, and promising to kick him out next time. This makes me question whether my initial reaction was over the top. 5. **Feeling Guilty**: I feel like an asshole if he was just playing a game, but I still don't want him to feel safe in the YMCA if he's causing discomfort to others. So, is it right or wrong for me to feel the way I did? Did I overreact? Or was I justified in feeling anxious and taking steps to ensure my safety? I think it's important to balance personal feelings with the facts. On one hand, I felt unsafe, and that's a valid feeling. On the other hand, the guy might have been innocently playing a game, which makes me question whether my reaction was appropriate. As for me, feeling anxious in such a situation is understandable, especially if I'm not comfortable confronting people directly. So, in conclusion, I don't think I'm being too harsh. It's also important for institutions like the YMCA to address such concerns to maintain a safe environment for everyone.
